1c630973f97d1a0251fa.text: Bias refers to an author’s expression of his/her own opinion on a particular

a21171d19a36b12fce76.text: issue without examining and presenting enough evidences. This arises from the author’s thinking which may be influenced by personal beliefs, culture, attitudes, preferences, and past experiences.

ca784a03bc4ba2100ada.text: When does an author become bias?

5697f28122bd10103354.text: An author becomes bias when he/she persuades the reader to believe on

c2ff01bee6b93a17186f.text: his/her own stand of the issue by giving inaccurate information or false impression even with or without the intention of misleading the readers.

980e898d9ada197df8c0.text: How do you determine the author’s biases?

30b6f804231c226b2ca0.text: To determine the author’s biases and to understand his/her underlying

5a01e6504c86a07264d8.text: purpose, you must look at the use of evidence and diction.

9401879f55e7d5de4b3b.text: observations, scientific and legal findings, and anecdotes and philosophical evidences.

d9dd9b62d680690ad085.text: In this part of the module, you will learn the meaning of literature, its

6fba46cd2bb9a03d76a0.text: elements, and how it reflects the culture of other group of people similar to your own.

94da72531dd6693ae7c2.text: Literature. It refers to a body of written works such as poetry, novels, history, biography, and essays that reflects the background of a certain culture. It is derived from the Latin word litaritura/litteratura which means “writing formed with letters.” There are a number of ways that literature is classified. The most basic types of literature are fiction and non-fiction.

f93f628fd91c409cb5a3.text: What are the Types of Literature?

26457bb2c83f796390f8.text: 1. Fiction. It is a type of literature that is a product of a writer’s imagination. It can be inspired by actual or completely made-up events. It is usually created through the use of clear details that we recognize or that move us in some ways.

a31709d8f3d950e209ca.text: The story “The Soul of the Great Bell” is a Chinese fiction retold in English by Lafcadio Hearn. The story is all about a girl named Ko-Ngai, a virgin maiden, who sacrificed her life to save her father Kouan-Yu from the anger of the Son of Heaven and Yung-Lo. Her blood was the main ingredient to successfully make the great bell. Another example of fiction is the “Story of the Aged Mother,” a Japanese folktale by Matsuo Basho. It is about a son and his mother going through struggles because of the unkind ruler who issued cruel orders which included among others, sending the elderly to the mountain to be abandoned and left to die. However, the son took good care of his mother. Meanwhile, the governor ordered that whoever could bring him a rope made of ashes would be honored. It was the mother’s wisdom that saved the entire town when the son revealed that it was his aged mother’s brilliant idea to make the order possible. The governor, in the end, denounced his previous order of killing all aged people.

8a175dc78849f2d31ffc.text: 2. Nonfiction. It is a type of literature that is based on facts. It is a writing about real people, places, and events which include biographies, auto-biographies, and interviews. Example: “Long Walk to Freedom” is an autobiography, a self-written story, of Nelson Mandela who was a South African activist and former president (1918-2013).

a5aeeafaa9a96fd2427d.text: What are the Elements of a Story?

a276aa6a5a61bbb38753.text: a. Exposition/Initial Action. This is the very beginning of a story. In this

09dfe23bbcc3b8d5b012.text: part, authors usually introduce the major characters and setting to the reader. In the illustration above, the author introduces the place Ayohdya as the setting and presents the characters King Dasharata, Rama, and Sita.

8849a7f1cfe9e08b6b9e.text: b. Rising Action. This is the part when tension starts to build. It usually

7b6af44281f883e7d87b.text: involves facing and conquering minor conflicts, which is what keeps the plot moving forward. In the illustration above, the tension started when Ravana devised a plan to abduct Sita.

91be471c8369e82fde40.text: c. Climax. This is the part of the story where the characters finally have to

This is the "peak" of the plot or the highest point of interest where all the tensions of the rising action lead to the success or failure of the hero. In the illustration above, Rama solved the major conflict when he fought and killed Ravana to save Sita.

b7fcc9fc637e8f41bbf5.text: e. Resolution/Denouement. This is the conclusion or ending of a story.

c3c162db2f50b9ccf133.text: 4. Conflict. It refers to the problem that the main characters have to face. The conflict of the story has four major types: man vs. man, man vs. self, man vs. society, and man vs. supernatural.

28d8cdf2da9f43aa43c3.text: 5. Point of View. This is the angle of narration or the perspective from which the story is told. It can be classified as first person and third person.

a4597cb86f0ddf507b88.text: a. First Person. The narrator is a character in the story who can reveal only

2d78d1cebb1ceb125aa0.text: personal thoughts and feelings. It uses the personal pronoun I. Example:

293cdad9710d4ca3d93b.text: “I was standing in the dark. I was scared and cold. Then, I felt something on

110b8da0b8d24af30491.text: b. Third person. This is when the narrator is removed from the story and tells

71dca0a7770babaf50f6.text: it from an outside perspective. To do this, the narrator uses personal pronouns like "he," "she," and "they" to refer to the characters in the story. Example:

fa25e327092a9869ee24.text: “Ravana devised a plan to abduct Sita. He sent a magical golden deer which

af4497121dd440130ba8.text: Sita desired Rama to hunt. A long time had passed, but Rama didn’t return. Thus, Lakshmana went off to find his brother.” - Ramayana

aca6166970dff19bde3f.text: Note: There are other types of point of view other than these two, but the first person point of view and the third person point of view are the common ones.

89dc31cb17097037227d.text: 1. Stay healthy and enjoy learning with us.

20a7a2ef6767801917e3.text: In the first sentence, the word “and” is used to add something to the previous

981d1252e1f83a36d7dc.text: idea. It connects the ideas of “Stay healthy” and “enjoy learning with us.” Also, you will notice that both statements start with verbs “stay” and “enjoy”. Thus, apart from using the word connector “and”, using parallel structures as seen in the example may be used to achieve cohesion.

fbc588528c57a6368600.text: 2. Therefore, we do not have to worry anymore.

4cfbf3c2a3bce9ba176f.text: In the second sentence, the word “therefore” is used to give or show

a263e8c2e11481587a7c.text: conclusion. With the efforts of the Department of Education with regards to students attending classes, Anna and her parents therefore, do not have to worry about her enrolment. Also, you will notice the use of the pronoun “we” which apparently refers back to Anna’s parents. The use of pronoun is also another cohesive device that you can take advantage. When you keep on referring to the same idea, it makes ideas stick together.

ae8162836d84b6cf733f.text: 3. However, my parents told me to stay home and stop schooling because they are concerned of my safety.

ad01005719ba896284bf.text: In the third sentence, the word “but” shows contrast of ideas. Also, the word

81f9d08acd163f37f3e9.text: “because” shows reason. So, in the sentence, because Anna’s parents are concerned of her safety.

a3e0c7e5162e993f6c73.text: Apart from using these connectors, it was also evident that there were a couple

bf83b7c943687a09cb0f.text: of repetitions evident in the dialogue. What words were repeated? The words school and stay were repeated. Also, the idea of the pandemic which was suggested by the following phrases the situation right now and pandemic are repeated. Thus, another way of achieving cohesion is through repetition of ideas or words.

19bd5182331c191a0411.text: This time, let us discuss more about cohesive devices.

1785c25d94803e434052.text: Cohesion in writing may be achieved through the following means: 1. Repetition of words or ideas. This helps to focus your ideas and to

275d3f17d45248c099f4.text: keep your reader on track. Example:

430c0f0c590765bd7ed2.text: Most people find contemporary art difficult to understand.

fe514531951406561cd4.text: Contemporary art is purposely abstract, leaving the viewers wondering what they are looking at.

9d2872c5259440ad7acb.text: 2. Use of synonyms for key words and phrases. Synonyms are words that have essentially the same meaning, and they provide some variety of word choices, helping the reader to stay focused on the idea being discussed. Example:

0c5c8075a2092c4feb5b.text: At the end of the run, he was suddenly afraid. The height of

40a0c17ad01c323d8203.text: 3. Pronouns / Determiners. This, that, these, those, he, she, it, they, and we are useful pronouns for referring to something previously mentioned. Be sure, however, that what you are referring to is clear. Example:

f9f5c475309734b7f030.text: Mr. Noviel Fraga is the CEO of Fraga Fisheries and Company.

7cd8330a25d003b0ff9b.text: 4. Use transitional devices (linkers, conjunctions or connectors). These are words which give cues to the readers on the relationships between sentences, joining sentences together.

f8758a4b9eec263ff601.text: The most common cohesive device used is the use of transitional devices. They

7c5f561cfc695cf318d1.text: are sometimes called linking words, linkers, connectors, or transitional words. These are words or group of words that show the relationship between sentences and paragraphs of a text or speech. These are words like ‘For example’, ‘In conclusion’, ‘however’, and ‘moreover’.

35bd42a9d66048f0b0fd.text: We use them to link sentences, paragraphs or any pieces of texts. In other

328631b23614debfbe7d.text: words, cohesive devices make our ideas coherent, consistent and organized. Inappropriate use of these can affect the flow of thoughts or ideas expressed in the sentence.

6d4bb92ce9e16444e18b.text: The common transition words are shown below.

421f6df73988c23ba0bf.text: Cohesive Devices     Type: Cohesive Devices Description Examples  Conjunctions 1. Coordinating Conjunctions These conjunctions connect words, phrases, and clauses of equal value. Clauses or equal value are called independent clauses and can stand on their own as separate sentence. for for explaining why He gains more weight, for he eats too much sweets.   and the same, similar or equal; without contrast His favorite snacks are apples and bananas.   nor for two non- contrasting grammatically, negative items He doesn’t like soft drinks, nor hard liquors.   but for contrast I eat vegetables, but I never eat junk foods.   or an alternative Would you like bread or cookies with your coffee?   yet contrast, despite, something He is still young, yet he is already very responsible.   so for showing the consequence of something He was very hungry, so he ate the remaining fruits.   because, so that, as, since to express cause or reason As he was feeling sick, Pedro didn’t go to work yesterday.

2. Subordinating Conjunctions The clause beginning with the subordinating conjunction is always the subordinate clause, which depends on the main clause and cannot exist without it.
before, after, until/till, when, as soon as, whenever, while
to express time
The baby cries whenever he feels hungry.
unless, if, even if, in case, providing
to express condition
I’ll lend you my phone, provided that you will use it carefully.
although, even though, whereas
to express contrast or concession
Joy loves outdoor activities, whereas her sister prefers to stay home.

3. Adverbial Conjunctions These are words that join independent clauses into one sentence. A conjunctive adverb helps you create a shorter sentence. When you use a conjunctive adverb, put a semicolon (;) before it and a comma (,) after it.
also, besides, finally, furthermore, in addition, moreover, still,
adding something
It rained hard; moreover, lightning flashed and thunder boomed.
also, as well, alike, similarly
comparing
Sleeping early makes me feel relax; also, makes me active for the next day.
at the same time, in contrast, in spite of, on the other hand even if
contrasting
I wanted to finish answering my activity in this module; even if, it takes longer time to do it.
certainly, definitely, indeed, in fact
emphasizing
Following health protocols is; indeed, very important for us to be safe.

a4896fc56e1975cc0c8a.text: To improve the clarity of your writing, it is important to remember the equality of your sentence structure. This module was designed to help you better understand the importance of Using Parallel Structures. Parallel Structure means using the same construction for sentence elements that are the same in function. Below are three rules to consider when checking for Parallel Structure in your writing: 1. Parallel Structure should be used when elements are joined by coordinating conjunctions:

c00b92177ee739e8db57.text: Incorrect: I am allergic to the dog’s hair and how it smells. Correct: I am allergic to the dog’s hair and smell.

4c2386fca1d2a83e295a.text: 2. Parallel Structure should be used when writing elements in the form of a list or a series:

d41181070c0b2cdceac8.text: Incorrect: The class valued respect, honesty, and being on time in a

0a1b71e024baa1dbf41e.text: Correct: The class valued respect, honesty, and promptness in a

8bad0c7ee5ba3512ee36.text: 3. Parallel Structure should be used when comparing or contrasting elements (A is better than B or X is less than Y):

5e7a76c055421cd883d7.text: Incorrect: James enjoys reading more than to write. Correct: James enjoys reading more than writing.

a56bcf85a48ad2e59db6.text: Note: If the sentence includes time signals that indicate the action

d0e93a9bc8434861cbb0.text: happening at different time or will happen in the future, disregard this rule.

88c981054278f0c700c1.text: Edna is an industrious student, an obedient daughter, and a loyal friend.

49ee3000c2d90dbc907f.text: In the use of parallel structure, grammatical balance should be observed. If parallel structure is not observed there will be a disruption of rhythm, thus there will be grammatical unbalance.

b7fdede2da165ea9292f.text: 1. Toni Gonzaga is a multi-talented celebrity. Singing, acting, and being a host are some of her talents. No error What do you think is the error in the sentence?

0f6ec4142eef73fb5a2d.text: You are correct! The answer is “being a host”, it is the error in the sentence.

5c976445a82bc5a76b9f.text: Explanation: In the list of talents that Toni Gonzaga has, two items are gerunds, or verbs being used as nouns ("singing" and "acting"), whereas "being a host" is a phrase. Thus, "being a host" does not fit with the parallel structure, and should be changed to "hosting.”

d4c3c7a7fd25f089c71c.text: 2. I live in a condominium on a higher floor than my boss. No error

5cb2740d201cb39d538d.text: What do you think is the error in the sentence?

61d44f70aa7604fd5df8.text: You are correct! The answer is “boss”, it is the error in the sentence.

c6f88c94c93c75825cd7.text: Explanation: Only like things can be compared. "My apartment" can be compared to "that of my boss" or my "boss”

fc4f96a3759f800783c1.text: Correct: I live in a condominium on a higher floor than my boss’

5ffe5945bae9499ac446.text: To use parallel structure in a sentence, words/phrases joined together by correlative conjunctions should be of the same grammatical level or structure.

dec1b10f9ff3fefee426.text: Wrong: The mall requires not only wearing face masks but also face

b91e35e4e263ce4f6167.text: Right: The mall requires wearing not only face masks but also face shields.

1d303ee4248614165bbc.text: In the example above the first part of the sentence, not only, joins the verb wanted. While the second part, but also, joins the direct object face masks. To achieve parallel structure, you must join two elements of the same grammatical level.

4de62737bac86db9ab1e.text: Neither - Nor Mistakes The elements joined together by correlative conjunctions should be equal to achieve parallel structure.

d28aaa7f4955a58bb162.text: Wrong: For the talent contest, she neither wanted to sing nor to

242b771a0240910758ad.text: Right: For the talent contest, she wanted neither to sing nor to

7f380602eec4603e7acb.text: Wrong: Either you answer your modules or attending online classes. Right: Either you answer your modules or attend online classes.
